_meta.indication: XCOPRI is indicated for the treatment of partial-onset seizures in adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group; two-arm (200 mg/day cenobamate vs placebo) with an 8-week baseline, 12-week treatment period (6-week titration and 6-week maintenance), and 1-week taper.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients aged 18-65 with treatment-resistant (refractory) partial-onset seizures, stable on 1-3 AEDs.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change in seizure frequency per 28 days in the treatment period compared to baseline.
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reduction in seizure frequency from baseline was 55.6% for cenobamate vs 21.5% for placebo; p<0.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 4-arm study (cenobamate 100, 200, 400 mg/day vs placebo) with an 8-week baseline, 18-week treatment period (6-week titration and 12-week maintenance), and 3-week taper.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults aged 18-70 with uncontrolled partial-onset seizures who failed at least 1 AED within 2 years, stable on 1-3 AEDs.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in seizure frequency per 28 days in the treatment period.
pivotal_trials.result: Median percent reductions from baseline in seizure frequency per 28 days were 55.3% (400 mg), 55.2% (200 mg), 36.3% (100 mg) vs 24.3% placebo; p-values vs placebo: 400 mg <0.001, 200 mg <0.001, 100 mg 0.006.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (at least 10% and more frequent than placebo) were somnolence, dizziness, fatigue, diplopia, and headache. In the pooled trials, at 400 mg/day somnolence occurred in 37% (vs 11% placebo) and dizziness in 33% (vs 15% placebo). The most serious risk is DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity (three cases in development, including one fatality); other notable risks are QT shortening and dose-dependent CNS adverse reactions.
target_moa: Cenobamate reduces repetitive neuronal firing by enhancing the fast and slow inactivation of sodium channels and by inhibiting the persistent component of the sodium current; it is also a positive allosteric modulator of six subtypes of the GABA_A ion channel. The exact mechanism of its anticonvulsant effect is not known.
modality: Small molecule (novel tetrazole-derived compound; new molecular entity)

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for the intended population.

summary.text: Cenobamate (Xcopri), a new molecular entity, was submitted November 21, 2018 and approved November 21, 2019 for treatment of partial-onset seizures in adults, supported by two adequate and well-controlled placebo-controlled trials. It was reviewed as a standard NDA under section 505(b); it was not referred to an advisory committee, and no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designations are stated in the documents.

citations.quote: The cenobamate drug substance (a novel tetrazole-derived compound with one chiral center) is a new molecular entity (NME) that is not currently approved in any country.
The efficacy of cenobamate was established by the results from two adequate and well-controlled clinical trials.

Your application for Xcopri was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable. The efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for the intended population.

requirement.text: 3712-10: Conduct a pregnancy outcomes study to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to Xcopri during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 3712-10 Conduct a pregnancy outcomes study using a different study design than provided for in the North American Antiepileptic Drug (NAAED) Pregnancy Registry (for example, a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data with outcome validation or a case-control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to Xcopri (cenobamate) during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3712-11: Perform additional nonclinical experiments to characterize the effects of cenobamate on the cardiac sodium channel, to determine the anti-arrhythmic sub-class of cenobamate.

citations.quote: 3712-11 Perform additional nonclinical experiments to characterize the effects of cenobamate on the cardiac sodium channel, which should allow for determining the anti-arrhythmic sub-class of cenobamate (i.e., la, lb, or lc).

requirement.text: 3712-12: Conduct a clinical pharmacokinetic trial to determine an appropriate dose of Xcopri to minimize toxicity in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

citations.quote: 3712-12 Conduct a clinical pharmacokinetic trial to determine an appropriate dose of Xcopri (cenobamate) to minimize toxicity in patients with severe hepatic impairment.
